title: Multimodal Co-learning: Challenges, Applications with Datasets, Recent Advances and Future Directions

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing the use of synthetic resume testbeds (FairCVtest) to test automated recruitment systems and probing pre-trained multimodal models (e.g., CLIP) on balanced datasets (like FairFace) to detect skewed representational associations, such as disproportionately classifying images of men as crime-related.

Reviewing evaluations of recruitment testbeds (FairCVtest) and probing multimodal representations (e.g., CLIP) using balanced datasets to identify biased associations, such as linking Asians to terrorism or testing the impact of masked ethnic information on algorithmic decisions.
Discussing the design of specific probes on pre-trained vision-language models to evaluate skewed geographic associations, such as disproportionately linking Latin America to immigration.
Reviewing the use of probing techniques and balanced demographic datasets (e.g., FairFace) to study representational biases across different age categories in multimodal models.
Highlighting the design of probes to study bias in multimodal models focusing on varying social conditions and how they skew model classifications.

Using counterfactual explanations (e.g., making text input absent or visual inputs distorted) to evaluate if models are unfairly biased towards a dominant modality (such as language) while ignoring clues from other modalities (like vision).
